name: Berkeley Castle
summary: The castle where Edward II died in captivity in 1327.
overview: Berkeley Castle in Gloucestershire became notorious as the place where the deposed Edward II died in captivity.
His death followed deposition, political collapse, and the rise of the regime around Isabella of France and Roger Mortimer.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Berkeley Castle was a fortified aristocratic residence whose fame in medieval history comes chiefly from Edward II’s imprisonment and death.

contentSections.title: Medieval historical context
paragraphs: Edward II died there in 1327 after being forced from the throne. The exact manner of death remains disputed, but the political context of custody and deposition is clear.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: The castle became part of one of medieval England’s darkest royal narratives: a king defeated by war, noble opposition, and palace politics.
